sentences.text:
2. This appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1973 against the award dated 21.07.2022 passed by 3rd Additional MACT, Nagod, District - Satna in MACC No.113/2021 for setting aside impugned award and grant of suitable compensation.
3.

Learned counsel for the appellants, after referring to para 10 and 11 of impugned award, submits that tribunal has wrongly dismissed appellant's claim petition on the ground that FIR has been registered after 10 days of accident.

Learned counsel for the appellants after relying upon Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayan and Others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, submits that a claim petition cannot be dismissed only on the ground of delay in lodging FIR.

entities.text:
Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayan and Others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, impugned award be set aside and suitable compensation be awarded.

4. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that tribunal has rightly dismissed appellant's claim petition after taking into consideration overall evidence on record and it has discussed and examined the same in the right prospective.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellants be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

6. It is correct that a claim petition cannot be dismissed only on the ground the delay in lodging/
FIR as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in Ravi (supra).
7.

Perusal of record of the case reveals that accident occurred on 23.4.2021 and FIR (Ex.P/2) has been registered on 04.05.2021 after marg enquiry.
8.
It is also evident from record of the case that sole eye witness examined by appellant is applicant witness no.2 Rambahori Choudhary.
As per deposition of Rambahori Choudhary, after accident, he went to the house of deceased's maternal uncle Vedmani Choudhary and informed him about the accident.
This witness has admitted in his cross examination that deceased Sonu is his grand-son and son of sister-in-laws of his daughter.
It is correct that he did not lodge report.
Witness voluntarily states that he had informed deceased's father about incident.
9. Thus, applicant witness Rambahori Choudhary has not lodged any FIR immediately after the accident.

It is evident from record of the case that deceased's maternal uncle Vedmani Choudhary also did not lodge any FIR after accident and after having received information about the accident Sanjeev Verma vs Rahul Dwivedi on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33631671/
2 from applicant witness Rambahori Choudhary.
Appellants have not examined Vedmani Choudhary.

10. Further, father of deceased, applicant witness Sanjeev Verma has admitted in para 8 of his cross examination that he had informed police that Rambahori Chodhary, resident of Patwara, had told him about the accident.
It is correct that Rambahori Choudhary just told him that his son had met with an accident.
Thus, this witness does not say that Rambahori Choudhary informed him about details of offending vehicle i.e. number etc. of offending vehicle.

Appellants have also filed statement recorded during marg inquiry and deceased's father's statement recorded during marg inquiry is Ex.P/13 and it has been recorded on the date of accident itself i.e. 23.4.2021.

In statement Ex.P/13,
it is mentioned that deceased's maternal uncle Vedmani Choudhary informed about the accident on telephone.
Therein, it is nowhere mentioned that applicant witness Rambahori Choudhary informed deceased's father about the accident and about details of offending vehicle.

11. In view of discussion in forgoing paras, applicant witness Rambahori Choudhary does not appear to be a reliable witness and it cannot be said that he witnessed the accident because he neither reported the matter nor deceased's maternal uncle Vedmani Choudhary nor deceased's father Sanjeev Verma had lodged the report against offending vehicle on the basis of information provided by applicant witness Rambahori Choudhary.
12.
Perusal of para 10 and 11 of impugned award reveals that tribunal had assessed and examined deposition of applicant witness Rambahori Choudhary in right perspective.
Therefore, in view of discussion in forgoing paras, it cannot be said that findings recorded by tribunal in paras 10, 11 and 12 are perverse or against evidence on record.
13. Hence, no interference is required in the findings recorded by tribunal whereby tribunal has dismissed appellant's claim petition.
14. Hence, appeal filed by the appellants is hereby dismissed.
